description: When CAP_REV or LM_SUBS genuinely resolves to 'NA' (curl timeout, empty body, non-JSON -- the python except-branch), and HEAL passed at check-time (or the heal-check endpoint differs from the read endpoint, so HEAL genuinely can't see this particular failure), STATUS falls through to the hardcoded default string at line 41: 'NO realised external revenue yet — bottleneck = DEMAND (users/sales), not code'. This is self-contradictory within the SAME STATE.md file: the same wake would show 'capafy_net_revenue_usd_3d: NA' or 'lm_active_paid_subs: NA' (a code/data-fetch failure indicator) right next to a STATUS line that explicitly asserts 'not code'. A human or the downstream self-improve agent skimming just the STATUS line would wrongly conclude there is no infra/code problem when in fact the READ step just failed.

evidence.snippet:
SPEND=200
STATUS="NO realised external revenue yet — bottleneck = DEMAND (users/sales), not code"
if printf '%s' "$CAP_REV" | grep -qE '^[0-9.]+$' && awk "BEGIN{exit !($CAP_REV>0)}" 2>/dev/null; then STATUS="EARNING (Capafy net \$$CAP_REV) — grow it"; fi
if printf '%s' "$LM_SUBS" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+$' && [ "${LM_SUBS:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then STATUS="EARNING (LM $LM_SUBS active subs) — grow it"; fi
[ -n "$HEAL" ] && STATUS="HEAL-NEEDED — $HEAL"

fix: Add an explicit branch: if CAP_REV=="NA" or LM_SUBS=="NA" (and HEAL is empty, i.e. HEAL didn't already catch it), set STATUS to something like 'READ-FAILED (NA) — data fetch broke after heal-check passed; investigate/retry', distinct from both EARNING and the demand-side default.
